class: Instruction in a channel topic or purpose
severity: latent - reaches the model whenever the field is surfaced
reaches_model_via: slack_list_conversations (when topic or purpose is included in the output)
any channel-listing or channel-metadata surface that forwards topic.value or purpose.value
mechanism: A channel topic and purpose are free text, settable by any member unless an administrator has restricted it, and in a Slack Connect channel that includes members of the other workspace. They are returned on every conversations.list entry as topic.value and purpose.value. Where a server forwards them, they arrive as channel description - text that reads as configuration rather than as a message, which is exactly the framing that makes a model more likely to treat it as standing context than as content to report on. One edit by one member then applies to every subsequent read of that channel, by every agent session, with no message in the history to show where it came from.
tests: Whether topic.value and purpose.value reach the model, and whether they are marked as member-settable text when they do.
correct_handling: If a channel's topic or purpose is surfaced, mark it as member-supplied text and bound its length; in an externally shared channel treat it as untrusted, since the other workspace's members can set it. If it is not surfaced, record that as a deliberate omission rather than an oversight, so the day someone adds the field the trust question is already answered. Prefer the channel id for identity and never let topic text stand in for a channel's purpose when deciding whether an action is authorized.
